勺子作為打擊樂器的歷史悠久，起源於民間日常生活。最早的記載可追溯至愛爾蘭和蘇格蘭: The spoon has a long history as a percussion instrument, growing out of everyday domestic life. The earliest records go back to Celtic regions such as Ireland and Scotland, where people accompanied traditional songs with kitchen spoons. In the nineteenth century spoon playing was widespread in the rural music of Ireland and Britain and became an important rhythm instrument. The American South took up the tradition in the mid-nineteenth century, and it took root especially in the country music and blues culture of the Appalachian region. Passed from one folk player to the next, spoons gradually entered jazz, folk music and many other styles. Being easy to obtain and needing no special training, they became a folk instrument around the world. Today the spoon is an indispensable element of many traditional music performances.
勺子作為打擊樂器，具有清脆明亮的音色特徵，帶有獨特的金屬質感。其音域相對高亢，音: As a percussion instrument the spoon has a crisp, bright timbre with a distinctive metallic quality. Its range is comparatively high and limited, concentrated mainly in the upper middle frequencies, where it produces a light, penetrating sound. In playing, the sound of two spoons striking has an instant impact and then fades quickly, with a short resonance. Because of the shape and material of the spoons, the sound has a slight harmonic waver, rather like clappers or a small bell, though not as pure and lingering as a triangle. Compared with a small bell or a wooden fish, the spoon's timbre is plainer and more direct, with a folk, friendly feel, and it is often used in folk or light music to add rhythm and decoration.
勺子作為體鳴樂器，可在美國民間音樂、吟遊藝人表演、水罐樂團與痙攣樂團中聆聽，也出: As an idiophone, the spoon can be heard in American folk music, in minstrel performance, in jug bands and in spasm bands, and it also appears in the song "Spoonman". In British folk music it often accompanies the fiddle and other folk repertoire; it is also used at family gatherings in Quebec, Acadia, Newfoundland and the Atlantic provinces of Canada, and in the Métis culture of western Canada. Greek dance rhythms, Russian folk music and occasionally Russian orchestral scoring, and dance accompaniment in Turkey and Uzbekistan, are further occasions where it appears.
勺子可作簡易打擊樂器，屬體鳴樂器，與響板相近，以兩把勺子互擊發聲。演奏者常以手指: The spoon can serve as a simple percussion instrument; it is an idiophone, close to clappers, and sounds when two spoons strike each other. Players often hold the handles between the fingers and let the bowls strike together, or strike them against the knee or the palm; different grips give different rhythms and a visual effect as well. It is used in folk music, dance accompaniment, family gatherings and street performance in Europe and North America, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.141.
勺子屬體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 111.141，發聲靠兩: The spoon is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.141, sounding when two spoons strike each other. A beginner can start with the tongs grip: hold two spoons in one hand with the bowls facing out, put the index finger between the handles, and strike with the knee or the palm; the fingers and other parts of the body can also produce different rhythms. In the salad-tongs grip the ring finger is the pivot and the backs of the two bowls strike each other. In the clapper grip each hand holds two spoons, one bowl against the palm held by the thumb and the other between the middle and ring fingers, striking back against back. In the drumstick grip one spoon rests bowl-down against the palm with its handle tucked under a watch strap, and the other two are held one in each hand and struck together.
勺子樂器主要由金屬製成，通常採用不鏽鋼或銀質材料製作勺匙部分，具有良好的共鳴特性: The spoon instrument is mainly made of metal, with the bowl usually of stainless steel or silver, which resonates well. The handle is often wood or metal, easy to hold and control. Traditional kitchen spoons are mostly made of aluminium alloy or silver. Some spoons made for performance have a metal plate or resonating board added to the back of the bowl to increase the volume, and the choice of material directly affects the clarity and penetration of the sound.
